title: Vitrified basalt blocks at Kef Kalesi confirmed by Schoch
place_text: Kef Kalesi, near Lake Van, Turkey

tellings.quote: melting that has taken place literal melting of the stone and Dr Robert Shaw confirmed confirmed on numerous stones that it is indeed vitrification

plain: A researcher of ancient sites named Matt LaCroix says the basalt stone blocks at Kef Kalesi, near Lake Van in Turkey, show "literal melting of the stone," and that the geologist Dr Robert Schoch confirmed on numerous stones that it is vitrification, meaning rock turned glassy by great heat. LaCroix tells it from his own visit, and if true it would mean the ancient walls were once hit by heat strong enough to melt rock.
